plan.planning_summary: Round 2 refines the previous 2-layer optimization (route_01) which achieved a target score of ~0.981 (mean reflectance ~0.019). The feedback directive explicitly suggests increasing the layer count to 3 to gain an additional degree of freedom for spectral shaping, as the 2-layer solution may be hitting a local optimum constrained by the fixed material set and thickness bounds. This route proposes a 3-layer stack (Air | L | H | L | Glass or Air | H | L | H | Glass) using the same SiO2/TiO2 materials. The topology is fixed to 3 finite layers to satisfy the 'fixed topology' rule while exploring the suggested design family expansion. Thicknesses are optimizable variables within the original 40-160 nm bounds.

routes.title: Expansion to 3-Layer SiO2/TiO2 Antireflection Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Adding a third layer to the two-material system (SiO2/TiO2) provides sufficient degrees of freedom to reduce the arithmetic mean reflectance over 450-700 nm below the ~0.019 level achieved by the optimal 2-layer configuration, potentially approaching the soft target of 0.03 with greater margin or exceeding it significantly.
routes.design_principle: Multi-layer impedance matching: A three-layer structure allows for a smoother transition of effective refractive index from air (1.0) to glass (1.52) across the bandwidth, mitigating the sharp resonances inherent in two-layer designs. Specifically, a Low-High-Low (LHL) or High-Low-High (HLH) sequence can broaden the antireflection band.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | Layer 1 | Layer 2 | Layer 3 | Glass Substrate. Total finite layers: 3. Material assignment hypothesis: Layer 1=SiO2, Layer 2=TiO2, Layer 3=SiO2 (LHL configuration).
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) over 450-700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: All layers must remain within 40-160 nm thickness bounds
Only SiO2 and TiO2 materials permitted
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory suggests that N-layer AR coatings can achieve lower average reflectance over a broad band than (N-1)-layer coatings given the same material constraints.
Quarter-wave stack principles adapted for broadband AR: centering optical thicknesses near lambda/4 at the geometric mean of the band edges.
expected_advantages: Broader spectral low-reflectance region compared to 2-layer design.
Lower arithmetic mean reflectance due to extra tuning parameter.
Potential to push mean reflectance well below 0.01.
known_risks: Optimizer may converge to a local minimum where the third layer has negligible effect (thickness near bound or effectively zero optical impact).
Increased complexity might lead to thinner layers approaching the 40 nm lower bound, increasing sensitivity to fabrication errors (though not modeled here).
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a planar 3-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52) with air incidence (n=1.0). The stack must consist of exactly three lossless constant-index layers in the order: SiO2 (n=1.46), TiO2 (n=2.40), SiO2 (n=1.46). Each layer thickness is a continuous variable bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm. Minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm (sampled every 5 nm). Use deterministic TMM. Initialize the optimizer with thicknesses corresponding to quarter-wave optical thickness at 575 nm (approx: 98nm, 60nm, 98nm) or random uniform within bounds. Run with seed 17, max 64 evaluations. Report the best candidate's thicknesses and resulting spectrum. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Follows feedback directive to increase layer count from 2 to 3 to explore if additional degrees of freedom can lower mean reflectance below the Round 1 result of ~0.019. Changes topology from 2 layers to fixed 3 layers (LHL).

research_influence: Feedback directive from Round 1 explicitly recommended increasing layer count to 3 to shape spectral response better.
Absence of literature evidence IDs forces reliance on theoretical basis for multi-layer AR design.
unresolved_decisions: Whether LHL or HLH ordering is superior for this specific index contrast (SiO2/TiO2/Glass); this route tests LHL only.
